name: Do You Need a Permit for a Garage Addition in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for a garage addition in Los Angeles County if the structure is detached from the house?
mainEntity.text: Do I need a permit for a garage addition in Los Angeles County if the structure is detached from the house?

acceptedAnswer.text: A detached garage addition usually still needs permits because local agencies review the structure’s size, placement, height, structural design, and utility connections. In Los Angeles County, requirements can vary by city and neighborhood, so a project that works in one area may need revisions in another. Setback compliance is especially important, along with roof height, lot coverage, drainage, and fire-rated construction if the garage is near a property line or another building. If the project includes electrical, plumbing, or future conversion potential, those items can trigger additional review. The best first step is to have a contractor check zoning rules before finalizing plans, because redesigning after submittal can add weeks or months. A contractor familiar with Los Angeles County can also help coordinate drawings, inspections, and plan corrections so the project moves more smoothly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, most garage additions in Los Angeles County require permits, even if the garage is detached. Permit review typically covers setbacks, height limits, fire separation, foundation plans, electrical work, and drainage. The exact requirements depend on the city, zoning rules, and whether the garage is new construction, an expansion, or a conversion.
